faq: What does this tool calculate?
Tile ground width = (equatorial circumference ÷ 2^zoom) × cos(latitude) — equivalently 256 × metres-per-pixel at that latitude.
Which map standard does it use?
The slippy-map standard (Web Mercator, 256-px tiles) shared by OSM, Google and MapLibre.
Can I use this in production GIS?
The formulas are the production standard itself — yes for web-mapping work.
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — tile systems are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — tiles and pixels quantise; decimals beyond the cell are decoration.
Why does latitude shrink tiles?
Mercator stretches the map poleward; the tiles cut uniform screen squares from a stretched map, so their ground footprint contracts by the same cosine.
Width at my exact tile?
A tile's width varies slightly across its own height (latitude changes within it) — the calculator uses the tile-centre latitude, the standard convention.
Area of a tile?
Width² approximately, locally — the conformal square makes area a one-line derivation.
Vector tiles same width?
Identical grid, identical ground width — vector versus raster changes content, not geometry.
Relating to scale bars?
A tile's width across a known screen size gives the display's true scale — the ground-width number is what scale bars are drawn from.
